title: Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software
summary:
The Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software is a Wikipedia article cataloging a wide range of open-source AI projects across multiple categories. Open-source AI, as defined by the Open Source Initiative, is an AI system that is freely available to use, study, modify, and share, including datasets used to train the model, its code, and model parameters.

The catalog includes cognitive architectures and general AI projects such as OpenCog, Soar, and CLARION. In game playing and logic, it covers KataGo for the game of Go and GOLOG for reasoning about action and change. Computer vision and robotics entries include AForge.NET, Dlib, and OpenCV.

Major machine learning and deep learning frameworks listed include TensorFlow, an end-to-end open-source platform for machine learning developed by Google Brain; PyTorch, a deep learning framework developed by Meta AI; Keras, a Python library for artificial neural networks integrated into TensorFlow; MXNet, a framework for training and deploying deep neural networks; and Caffe, a deep learning framework focused on speed and modularity. Neural network entries include FANN, AlexNet, VGGNet, Nengo, and OpenNN.

Natural language processing tools listed include Spark NLP, Word2vec, the Hugging Face transformers library of pretrained transformer models, Fairseq from Facebook AI Research, OpenNMT for neural machine translation, and Common Crawl. Data mining and AutoML entries include Orange for machine learning and data visualization, and MindsDB for embedding machine learning into SQL databases.
